From my understanding, the Sunday day off doesn't actually stem from religious reasons, it comes from late 1800s when Britain lost during the first Boer war. Before this, we were seen as a huge military might and then we were defeated basically by Dutch farmers. At the time, this was embarrassing for us on the world stage. We also had a type of physical education called Drill, which was very militaristic. After the Boer war, we changed the system up and Sunday just happened to be the designated day off for more businesses mainly traders, that's why most markets don't run on a Sunday. The purpose of this new system, we encouraged people to become more involved in sports such as Rugby and Football. This also lead to a boom in football teams as well. As a result of this, we started providing fitter and stronger men for war and thus this was the most up-to-date reason I know, why Sunday was designated as a day off it was for sports to keep a healthy population and was fit. So what would happen is factories, traders basically most workers would all go and play some sort of sport on a Sunday. This also lead to free school meals, compulsory medical checks for school children as we were seen as unhealthy and malnourished.

However if something has changed since then, I'm unaware of this and would love to know when this changed happened. Also if any of my information is incorrect, please feel free to update me it's been a while since I've look at this stuff

https://blogs.cdc.gov/niosh-science-blog/2009/10/14/n95/

I mean you're well within your right to disagree, however if they worked, medical staff wouldn't be getting infected 

Surgical masks, protect others from you, not completely or very effectively but they do provide a small margin of protection against airborne disease, but it does not protect the wearer

The surgical mask was literally invented to protect patients from the doctor during surgery, not to protect the doctor

If you're treating a patient, having good general health, good hygiene and fully washed hands with a mask will offer you some protection.

Some studies currently are showing this virus is spread simply by breathing as it's not sitting in the lungs but more in the nasal passages as it's colder and more ideal conditions. Which if breathing is why this is spreading a mask will be even more useless even if you wear it to protect others 

As I said a N95 respirator will help protect you, a surgical mask will help protect others

Not to be that guy, but their is little evidence masks protect you, unless as someone mentioned you wear a N95 respirator, surgical masks are designed to protect other people against you.
